title: DEVELOPMENT OF A DISSOLUTION TEST METHOD FOR CAPSULES OF A NEW ORIGINAL COMPOUND GML-3 WITH NEUROPSYCHOTROPIC ACTIVITY AND ITS VALIDATION
abstract: Introduction. GML-3 is a new compound first synthesized at the Federal State Budgetary Scientific Institution "Federal Research Center for Innovator and Emerging Biomedical and Pharmaceutical Technologies," which is a TSPO ligand and exhibits pronounced neuropsychotropic activity. On its basis, a solid dosage form was developed - capsules, one of the main methods for assessing the quality of which is the "Dissolution" test, which allows characterizing the drug product not only from a technological, but also from a biopharmaceutical point of view. The aim of this study was to select the optimal conditions for the dissolution test and to develop and validate a quantitative analytical method for GML-3 for this test. Material and methods. The objects of the study are an experimental samples of the substance N-butyl-N-methyl-1-phenylpyrrolo[1,2-a]pyrazine-3-carboxamide (under the laboratory code GML-3) and TDLF GML-3 (capsules with a dosage of 1 mg). The dissolution test was performed using a Phar-ma Test DT 70 device (Vitec, Germany) with interchangeable paddle stirrers, at a dissolution medium temperature of 37 °C ± 0.5 °C and a stirring speed of 50 rpm. The degree of release of GML-3 from the capsules into the dissolution medium was evaluated using the UV-spectrophotometry method on a UV-1700 spectrophotometer (Shimadzu, Japan), in a quartz cuvette with a layer thickness of 10 mm (Hellma 100-QS, Hellma Analytics, Germany). Results. The release kinetics of GML-3 from a new solid dosage form (capsules) was studied. A dissolution medium was selected, and the optimal conditions for conducting dissolution test for GML-3 capsules were chosen. A quantitative determination analytical procedure by UV spectrophotometry was developed, and its validation was carried out for the key validation parameters. Conclusions. Optimal conditions were chosen for performing the study “Dissolution” for capsules GML-3. Analytical methodology was designed and validated for quantitative assessment of GML-3 release from capsules. Methodology for the “Dissolution” test of the drug GML-3, capsules 1 mg was developed on the base of the obtained experimental data.
